input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence grant (Section 4(c), covering Contractor's Information embedded in the Works) runs to "Company" alone: affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not named, the grant is not stated to be irrevocable, and it is not transferable (Section 10 bars assignment without consent, so no successor path). It is perpetual and includes sublicence rights, so the gap is narrower than walk-away, but it falls short of the preferred position. Redline adds affiliates and contractors, "irrevocable", and transferability to a successor to our business or assets; fallback is affiliate coverage on notice with M&A successor transfer only.

proposal.summary: Extend Contractor's Information licence to Company affiliates and contractors, make it irrevocable and transferable to a successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended this licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and made it irrevocable and transferable to a successor, so the delivered Works remain usable across our group and after any reorganisation. If preferred, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice with transfer limited to a successor in an M&A transaction.

ops.oldText: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense)
ops.newText: Contractor hereby grants to Company, its affiliates (any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Company) and contractors acting on Company's behalf a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable license, transferable to a successor to Company's business or assets (including the right to grant a sublicense)
